UHSR EXAMINATIONS
ANQP Code: MBY2P5 Q.P. Code: 1725N
10th September, 2026 MBBS 2nd Prof.
Time: 3 hours M. Marks: 100 Pharmacology (Paper-1) Roll No..2.0.7..2..8 9
*AR IMPORTANT NOTE:
1. Attempt all of the following questions. Preferably attempt all the questions serially.
2. Part-A and Part-B are to be attempted in separate answer booklets.(Two answer booklets to be used)
3. Do not leave blank spaces of more than two lines in the writing area on the answer sheet, cross
any blank spaces of more than two lines before the END stamp after you finish the exam.
4. Do not use black lead/graphite pencil on the answer booklets for answering the questions.
A case of use of Unfairmeans will be made if instructions at 2, 3 & 4 are not complied.
PART-A
Q.1 A 40-year-old farmer presented to the emergency with complaints of abdominal cramps, vomiting, 3+3+3+2=11
diarrhoea and breathlessness. On examination there was drooling of saliva, constricted pupils, moist
skin and rapid pulse with slow volume. It was diagnosed as a case of organophosphate poisoning.
(a) Write down the pharmacotherapy for this patient.
(b) Write down the pharmacological basis of prescribed drugs.
(c) Why Oximes are not effective for carbamate poisoning?
(d) Enumerate other uses of antimuscarinic drugs.
Q.2 Write short notes on: 5x5=25
(a) Pharmacotherapy of Status asthmatics
(b) Adverse effect and contraindications of beta blockers
(c) Kinetics of elimination
(d) Role of low dose aspirin for coronary artery disease
(e) Principles of bioethics
Q.3 Explain why? 3x3=9
(a) Dopamine is preferred over Adrenaline for the treatment of cardiogenic shock.
(b) Volume of distribution of certain drugs exceeds total blood volume.
(c) Thrombolysis should be done as early as possible, within first few hours after myocardial infarction
Q.4 Multiple choice questions. 1x5=5
1. A 58-year-old woman with hypertension and paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia
requires a calcium channel blocker that balances peripheral vasodilation with AV node
conduction slowing. Which benzothiazepine derivative is most appropriate?
(a) Nifedipine
(b) Verapamil
(c) Diltiazem
(d) Nicardipine
2. A 32-year-old Caucasian woman experiences chest pain with exertion. She reports having
similar episodes in the past. It is determined that she is experiencing stable angina. She is
given nitro-glycerine to relax her vascular smooth musculature. Which best describes a
step on nitro-glycerine's mechanism of action?
(a) Activation of adenylate cyclase
(b) Activation of guanylate cyclase
(c) Inhibition of calcium channels
(d) Inhibition of cGMP phosphodiesterase
3. Why is the onset of action of lidocaine delayed in infected tissue?
(a) Increased hepatic clearance
(b) Decreased un-ionized drug available to cross the nerve membrane
(c) Rapid degradation by tissue esterases
(d) Downregulation of voltage-gated sodium channels
4 62-year-old man with congestive heart failure has been taking a loop diuretic to reduce
peripheral edema. His labs reveal a serum potassium of 3.1 mEq/L, so a potassium-sparing
diuretic, triamterene, is added to his regimen. Which of the following is the site of action of
this agent?
(a) Thick ascending limb of loop of Henle
-(b) Collecting tubule
(c) Proximal Convoluted Tubule
(d) Cortical diluting segment of loop of Henle
